hpi: {{patient_name}} presents with new-onset chest pain at rest lasting >20 minutes, or accelerating pattern of previously stable exertional angina. ECG shows ischemic ST depression or T-wave inversion — no ST elevation (distinguishes from STEMI). Troponin is negative or minimally elevated (distinguishes from NSTEMI). UA is part of the acute coronary syndrome spectrum: USA = ischemia without infarction. Pathophysiology: atherosclerotic plaque rupture → subtotal thrombus → decreased coronary flow but not complete occlusion. Management: anti-ischemic therapy (oxygen if hypoxic, nitroglycerin, morphine), antiplatelet (aspirin 325mg chew + P2Y12 inhibitor — ticagrelor or clopidogrel), anticoagulation (UFH or LMWH or fondaparinux), beta-blocker (unless contraindicated), high-intensity statin, ACE inhibitor. Risk stratify: TIMI or GRACE score. Early invasive strategy (cardiac catheterization within 24h) for high-risk features. Admit to monitored bed.
